messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: high rate of GPU driver resets detected in region us-west-2 (node group: gpu-pool-3). Xid-type errors spiking across multiple hosts. Error-rate increase 5xx->12% in inference route /v1/generate. Graph: https://telemetry.redwood/internal/alerts/3432109876

maria: seeing the same. telemetry shows Xid count jumping at 15:03 UTC across 3 hosts. can someone grab dmesg + nvidia-smi output?

devon: grabbing now. affected nodes: gpu-03-7, gpu-03-9, gpu-03-12. nvidia-smi shows driver reset messages. dmesg snippet:```
[2026-03-15T15:02:54Z] NVRM: Xid (13): Pri 0, 0000:03:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[2026-03-15T15:02:54Z] kernel: nvidia: GPU reset detected on device 0000:03:00.0
[2026-03-15T15:03:01Z] NVRM: Xid (61): Unrecoverable ECC error
```

alex: also seeing KV cache OOMs on some runtime containers immediately after driver reset. container log (tail):```
[15:03:05] runtime: kvcache reclaim failed, OOM while allocating 256MB
[15:03:06] inference: error writing kvcache chunk, closing session
```

maria: impact estimate: about 8% of inference capacity in us-west-2 is degraded; error-rate on the hosted API for a handful of mid-tier customers spiked. Not at full outage yet but increased retries and tail latency.

ops-lead: plan: 1) cordon + drain the 3 most noisy hosts, 2) failover traffic for affected routes to us-east-1/dedicated-fallback pool, 3) reboot and reprovision drained hosts with older driver build (525.105.x) if resets persist. following runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-reset (step 2: emergency-evac).

devon: running drain now on gpu-03-9 and gpu-03-12. command:```
kubectl cordon gpu-03-9 && kubectl drain gpu-03-9 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl cordon gpu-03-12 && kubectl drain gpu-03-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

support-lead: opening customer bridge for potentially impacted customers. bridge url: https://bridge.redwood/customer/BR-9821 (creating now). tagging support rotation and adding ops. @support-lead taking lead on comms.

customer-bridge-bot: Bridge created: BR-9821. Participants: support, ops-lead, devon. Use this channel to post status updates to customers.

alex: diag note: when the driver resets happen, the runtime's KV cache keeps handles open; some pods hit memory fragmentation and OOM. short-term mitigation: restart runtime pods on drained nodes prior to uncordon, and reduce KV cache max-size to 512MB in config to limit reoccurrence.

maria: confirming that rollback to driver 525.105.17 (tested in canary earlier) removed similar reset patterns in our staging cluster. ops-lead, can infra schedule driver reimage after drain?

ops-lead: yes. we will schedule reboot+reimage on the 3 drained hosts with driver 525.105.17. expected time per host ~6 mins. will bring back one at a time and watch Xid counters.

devon: drained gpu-03-9 -> pods evacuated. starting reboot of gpu-03-9 now. monitoring error-rate and inference SLOs.

incident-bot: Update: Xid spike subsided on gpu-03-9 after reboot; Xid count down to baseline. Overall 5xx rate decreased from 12% -> 6% for the affected routes.

maria: good. continuing with gpu-03-12 next. also triggering a temporary routing policy to reduce batch sizes on us-west-2 hostpool to limit memory pressure: set batch.max_tokens=256 for /v1/generate on us-west-2 for 30m.

support-lead: posted initial note to customers on bridge: "Experiencing elevated errors for some requests in us-west-2 due to GPU driver resets. We are actively evacuating affected hosts and routing traffic to fallback pools. We'll post updates every 15 minutes." :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alex: after restart on gpu-03-9 we observed some repaired nodes still emitting occasional Xid (minor). recommending increased telemetry sampling for ECC counters and enabling early-oom-signal to the runtime so that we can preempt heavy KV allocations on noisy GPUs. filing infra task.

ops-lead: gpu-03-12 reboot done, no recurrence so far. bringing back to service post-checks. still holding gpu-03-7 as next candidate—it's the heaviest noisy.

devon: gpu-03-7 shows sustained Xid messages; plan to evacuate and reprovision with older driver. starting drain in 60s.

maria: quick check: total impacted hosts 3/120 in us-west-2. capacity degradation ~8% but fallthrough routing prevented customer-visible outage beyond increased latency/retries for some customers.

incident-bot: Post-update: all three noisy nodes drained and reprovisioned with driver 525.105.17. Xid counters returned to baseline. Monitoring 30m before closure.

support-lead: informing customers on bridge that issue is mitigated and we're monitoring. asking SRE to prepare a short post-incident note for affected customers.

ops-lead: action items assigned: 1) infra to run a fleet sweep for nodes with driver 525.106+ and high ECC counts (owner: alex), 2) runtime to add defensive cgroup/memory limits to kvcache (owner: maria), 3) create emergency runbook update for noisy-driver-reset (owner: devon).

maria: adding eval to Redwood Optimize to watch output/regressions caused by lower batch sizes and reduced KV cache.

devon: moving this thread to oncall-handoff. handing off to infra for follow-up and postmortem.

ops-lead: severity: SEV3 (partial degradation, customer impact limited). creating incident record: INC-2026-03-15-01. please add any additional notes to the incident doc.

maria: noted. I'll follow up with telemetry dashboards and attach relevant dmesg/log snippets to the postmortem.

support-lead: closing customer bridge in 20m if no further regressions. thanks everyone for quick coordination. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-03-15-01: transition to monitoring. Last update at 15:45 UTC.

devon: closing thread here, will file a full postmortem and link to INC-2026-03-15-01.

maria: thanks all.
